text: Hook loop starts fresh when the context grows large: cache reads of a long context are most of a turn's cost
description:
OBSERVED 2026-11-24 from session-costs.log (2b55e8c3), 20 priced turns of one long Claude Code session driven by the Stop hook: median 2.91M cache-read tokens and 3.4k output tokens per turn, median $0.69 per turn (API-equivalent, claude-opus-5-5 list prices); 82% of the cost is cache reads. Each model call in a turn re-reads the whole context (about 400k tokens late in this session), so cost per turn grows with session length, not with the work.

INFERRED: with a context of ~60k the same turns would read ~1/7 as much, ~$0.20 per turn. The loop keeps its state in the space and git (not in the conversation), so a fresh session loses little.

Proposal: the Stop hook (or the recorder, which already reads the usage) notices when the last turn's reads per call pass a threshold (e.g. 250k) and says so in its block reason: commit, write the progress line, then end so the human (or a wrapper) restarts with a fresh session; or the wrapped-agents watchdog restarts it. Measure $/turn before and after.

Refuted if a fresh session spends so much re-orienting (reading the space, code) that cost per finished idea doesn't drop.

status.comment: Found from the first cost data; not discussed with Felix yet.
